description:
FILED s538a (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-12) beside #3618.  #3618 (s538a) made every OPENER's install slot (`%p-fh-place-check`: open, sysopen, opendir, pipe, socket, accept) die "Not a GLOB reference" for a box holding a reference that is not a handle (`%p-stat-handle-shaped-p` false, `ref` non-empty).  The USE slots are the same rule in perl (rv2gv) and were not touched.

REPRO (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL on main 23f0f917 and the s538a tree alike; scratch/s538a/pr/useslot.pl in the s538a worktree):
    my $x = sub { 42 }; my $o = \$x;
    print $o "hi" / printf $o "%s", "hi" / print {$o} "hi" / close $o /
    my $l = <$o> / eof($o) / binmode $o / fileno($o)
  perl: every one dies "Not a GLOB reference"; PCL: every one returns ("ok"), the print writing nowhere visible.

FIX SHAPE (not started): the handle-USE resolution (`%p-fh-arg` / `%p-resolve-fh`, the print family's `:fh` slot) asks the same two facts %p-fh-place-check asks -- a box whose payload is not handle-shaped and whose `ref` is non-empty -- and dies.  CAUTION before widening: find every PCL representation that a handle slot legitimately receives (IO::Scalar / IO::String objects, tied-handle objects, a dirhandle, a socket object, a blessed glob) and probe each vs perl; `%p-stat-handle-shaped-p` is the one designator predicate.  BAR: the eight rows above + the controls (a glob, a glob ref, an open lexical handle, a blessed IO::Handle, a tied handle) vs perl; a Pl/t row beside Pl/t/open-modes-01.t row 11; the FULL sweep (a `cl/` handle-resolution change).
subject: SILENT WRONG (pre-existing): a handle USE slot (print / printf / print {...} / close / readline / eof / binmode / fileno) given a variable holding a NON-HANDLE reference (`\$code`) runs silently ("ok"); perl dies "Not a GLOB reference" in every one -- #3618 fixed only the OPENER (install) slot
